reason: The load-bearing claim is a measurement error. Driving master.html?state=print in chromium at 1440 and probing true baselines with a zero-height inline-block strut: .b-num first baseline = 264.19 and .b-unit FIRST baseline = 264.19 - identical to the pixel. The finding's 294.97 is .b-unit's LAST baseline; the 30.78px 'drift' it reports is exactly 2 x the 15.4px line box (11px/1.4) of a three-line wrap, not a lost alignment. Screen and print are structurally the same: .b-count is align-items:baseline in both, and the num line-box-to-unit line-box delta is 108.00px in owner-flight and 108.00px in print. Nothing left any baseline. The '21px below the numeral' is likewise just the 2nd and 3rd wrapped lines hanging under a 133.2px line box, which is what a baseline-aligned caption stack does by definition. Second, the fix is already handled, more carefully than proposed. It asks for 'the date span carrying white-space:nowrap'; fixture.js line 55 already welds the date with U+00A0 (NB) in fmt.longYear, and the comment above it records the exact experiment: 'Binding the WHOLE string overflows its column on a phone and on the printed sheet, which is why only this one joint is welded.' I reproduced that - forcing white-space:nowrap on .b-print .b-unit sets one 239.4px line that overflows the 300px column by ~110px into the gutter. Third, the fix does not do what it claims. With the left column widened to 300px the unit slot becomes 129.6px and the unit STILL sets three lines at 84.5/56.3/84.5, because the welded date is an unbreakable 84.5px token; you would need a ~318px column before 'days away on Thursday' fits, and the result is a 147.8/84.5 rag, not 'two even lines'. Fourth, the fix makes the sheet worse elsewhere: .b-two is 220px + 48px gap + 412px inside a 794px A4 page, so +80px on the left is -80px on the measure, and at 332px the first title ('Menu tasting at The Orchard') breaks to two lines - it is one of seven titles that all currently set on one line, so the fix trades a non-defect for a real break in the measure's rhythm. (For the record on the brief's key risk: neither variant paginates - deepest content sits 916.9px into the 1123px sheet as-is and 894.4px with the 300px column - so pagination is not what kills this, the facts are.) Fifth, the .b-gapNote 'measure floor' argument is a category error. The box is 220px (~24ch at 15px), not 17ch; the string 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' measures 220.08px, i.e. it misses one line by 0.08px, and .b-gapNote carries text-wrap:pretty, which is why it breaks as 'Nothing is planned' / 'until 1 August.' (124.6/92.0) instead of widowing 'August.' alone. That is the rag engine doing its job on a 34-character sentence in a sidebar column - there is no continuous prose here for a 45-75ch measure floor to apply to. What is left after all that is a taste preference for a two-line caption over a three-line one, in an 84px mono slot that the frame shows reading cleanly as a deliberate stack tucked into the numeral's shoulder.
sharpenedFix: Nothing to fix. If a future round still dislikes the three-line stack, the only change that would not cost the measure column is at the copy layer, not the layout: drop the weekday from the print unit so it reads 'days away on 16 July 2026' (two lines, 84.5/84.5, no column change, weekday still present in the 'Today, Thursday 16 July 2026' origin line in the right column). Do NOT widen .b-two's left column - it is a zero-sum trade against the measure on a fixed 794px sheet.
